concepts.label: Sub-Document MUTATEIN operation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new: couchbase.mutateIn() with MutateInSpec.insert/replace/remove is the CAS-free write-side sibling of eventing:lookupin-subdocument-operation (the read-side operation minted in round 8's Capella twin); no existing concept in the registry or in round 8's cloud/eventing extractions covers this write-side mechanism under this name - round 8's own twin for this page left concepts/relations empty, treating it as a recurrence of an 'already covered' mechanism, but the covering concept it pointed to (the eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md doc page) was never itself minted as a concept id anywhere in the extraction pool that this batch's context surfaced

relations.subject: server/8.0/eventing/eventing-handler-advancedMutateInField
relations.evidence: For more information about the Advanced Sub-Document MUTATEIN operation , see [Sub-Document MUTATEIN Operation](eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md#advanced-subdoc-array-op-mutatein).

notable_absence.finding: 'Demonstrates the CAS-free Sub-Document MUTATEIN operation on a document field' - the CAS-free framing pairs directly with eventing:cas-conditioned-delete/advancedReplaceOp's CAS-conditioned whole-document operations elsewhere in this batch: sub-document MUTATEIN and whole-document REPLACE/DELETE sit at opposite ends of the same CAS-optionality axis, but no existing predicate expresses 'lacks the CAS-conditioning that a sibling operation has', so this is recorded as a finding rather than a relation. Per the round context's instruction on sdk:subdocument-operations reuse: not linked here for the same reason as advancedLookupInOp.json - the page never mentions the SDK's own subdocument API, so there is no page evidence to support a relation to it.
